Panama’s history — Los Canaleros have grown into a genuine CONCACAF force, reaching the 2023 Gold Cup final and a 2025 Nations League final. Captained by record cap-holder Anibal Godoy, this experienced squad arrives with belief rather than mere gratitude.
[...]
Panama are the clear outsiders in Group L, ranked well below England and Croatia. The expanded 48-team format, where the four best third-placed teams advance, offers a slim but real lifeline. Their realistic target is the match against Ghana on June 17 in Toronto — likely the game that defines whether they can compete for a knockout spot.
[...]
For Panama, simply being competitive and avoiding the winless, pointless return of 2018 would mark progress. A win — their first-ever at a World Cup — would be a historic achievement, and sneaking into the round of 32 would be a national triumph.
[...]
Under Thomas Christiansen, Panama are organised, disciplined and pragmatic. Expect a compact defensive block, deep lines against superior opponents, and a reliance on counter-attacks, set-pieces and the leadership of Godoy and Carrasquilla. Christiansen’s long tenure has instilled a clear identity and team cohesion that punches above the squad’s individual quality. The trade-off is limited creativity in sustained attack against deep blocks; Panama are at their best when defending a structure and breaking at speed.
[...]
Panama’s World Cup story is short but emotional. Their debut at Russia 2018 followed a famous qualifying campaign
[...]
ended in national celebration. The tournament itself was a brutal lesson at
[...]
elite level:
[...]
- Underdog romance — a small nation chasing its first-ever World Cup win and point.
- The England rematch — redemption beckons against the side that beat them 6–1 in 2018.
- Passionate support — “La Marea Roja” brings colour, noise and emotion to every match.
- Giant-killer potential — a well-drilled, experienced side that can frustrate the favourites.
[...]
Spirited group-stage campaign — a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.
[...]
Panama are the outsiders to qualify from Group L. Their season hinges on the opener against Ghana — a result there could keep alive hopes of a best-third-place finish in the expanded format. More likely, Panama will be competitive but fall short of the knockout rounds, with a maiden World Cup win or point representing genuine success. Projected: spirited group-stage campaign; a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.

Even in an optimistic scenario where Panama do advance, they would likely face a top-seeded side in the round of 32. A run to the quarter-finals would represent one of the tournament’s most remarkable stories. For betting purposes, the outright winner price at 1000/1 to 1500/1 reflects the near-impossibility of that scenario materialising. The stage-of-elimination market, specifically group-stage exit, represents where the realistic value sits.

The most grounded position on Panama at these World Cup odds is backing them to exit at the group stage. Group L contains England and Croatia alongside Ghana, and while Panama’s unbeaten qualifying record (5W 3D 0L, 14 goals scored, 4 conceded) demonstrates genuine defensive organisation, the step up in class is substantial. Panama’s best chance of a surprise result comes against Ghana, but even claiming maximum points there would leave them needing something from either Croatia or England. Group-stage exit is the most likely scenario and should be available at short odds reflecting that probability.
